caption:
Why can no one read the Voynich manuscript? A 600-year-old book written in an alphabet that matches nothing on earth — and after more than a century of professional codebreakers, not one line has been deciphered.

The vellum was radiocarbon dated to between 1404 and 1438. The iron gall ink and the pigments match the period, which rules out a modern forgery. Whatever it is, somebody really made it in the early 15th century.

Inside: plants that match nothing that grows, circular diagrams that look astronomical, and page after page of flowing script that behaves like a real language and belongs to none.

Wilfrid Voynich bought it in 1912. Pages were already missing by then. It now sits in Yale's Beinecke Library as MS 408.

What is still open: everything. A lost language, an unbroken cipher, or an elaborate hoax — nobody has proved which.

Images: Beinecke Rare Book & Manuscript Library, Yale. Public domain.
